sourceReferences.note: Word bank identical to official page 1 word bank (12/12).

learningObjectives: Listen to and enjoy the first-day-of-school poem and sing it with actions.
Recognise and say the 12 poem words from the 'Look and say' bank: see, skip, walk, grin, bell, rings, jump, play, school, Grade, everyone, hurray.
Connect each action word (skip, run, walk, jump, play) to a physical action.
Speak one line about coming to school using a poem word with teacher support.
prerequisiteSkills: No prior English assumed; KG Alphabet Garden (g00) levels are helpful but optional.
Can repeat a spoken word after the teacher.
Comfortable with turn-taking in a shared-lab setting.

vocabulary.sourceRef: 1.1 poem line 'See me run', printed p.1

phonicsConcepts: Hear the difference between action words by doing them: skip vs jump vs walk.
Hear the long 'ee' sound in see and everyone.
Clap syllables: sk-i-p (1), e-ve-ry-one (4).

grammarConcepts.concept: 'I am' + feeling/action in speech (I am in Grade One)
grammarConcepts.childFriendlyFraming: Special letters a-e-i-o-u help make words; 'I' always wears a capital letter because it is you.

comprehensionGoals: Point to the correct picture/action when Miss Julie says a poem word.
Answer 'What does the child do when the bell rings?' by acting, then by saying 'go in' or 'school'.
speakingObjectives: Say any 6 of the 12 word-bank words clearly enough for a peer to act them out.
Recite one remembered poem line pair with actions (student's own choice of remembered line).

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Act-it-out flashcards
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Six large flashcards (skip, walk, run, jump, play, grin) — student picks a card, everyone acts.

suggestedVisualActivities.title: School-bell soundscape
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Play a school bell sound; students shout 'The bell rings!' and march in a circle.

suggestedVisualActivities.title: First-day picture walk
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Friendly classroom illustration with hidden word-bank items to point at and name.

teacherExplanationExamples.en: Skip is walking with a happy little hop — one, two, one, two. Can your feet try it?
teacherExplanationExamples.hi: Skip यानी उछलकर चलना — एक, दो, एक, दो। क्या आपके पैर कोशिश करेंगे?
teacherExplanationExamples.mr: Skip म्हणजे उड्या मारत चालणे — एक, दोन, एक, दोन. तुमची पाये प्रयत्न करतील का?

teacherExplanationExamples.en: When the bell rings, we go inside. Ding-dong — that is the bell!
teacherExplanationExamples.hi: घंटी बजती है तो हम अंदर चले जाते हैं। डिंग-डॉंग — यही घंटी है!
teacherExplanationExamples.mr: घंटा वाजतो तेव्हा आपण आत जातो. डिंग-डॉन्ग — हाच घंटा!

hindiExplanations: स्कूल का पहला दिन — बच्चे नाचते, कूदते और खुश होते हैं। हम भी कविता के शब्दों के साथ अंग-संचालन करेंगे।
Grin यानी खुले दाँतों वाली मुस्कान। Bell यानी घंटी — स्कूल में जब घंटी बजती है, हम कक्षा में चले जाते हैं।
marathiExplanations: शाळेचा पहिला दिवस — मुले उड्या मारतात, धावतात आणि आनंदाने हसतात. आपण कवितेच्या शब्दांसोबत हालचाली करू.
Grin म्हणजे दात दिसेल असे हसणे. Bell म्हणजे घंटा — शाळेत घंटा वाजला की आपण वर्गात जातो.
expectedStudentAnswers: Single words from the bank: skip, jump, school, bell…
Action instead of a word (acting out skip) — accept, then model the word.
'I go to school.' / 'I am in Grade One.' with L1 support words mixed in.
Hindi/Marathi gloss first: 'seb'/'सफरचंद' pattern — accept, translate, re-model in English.

adaptiveTeachingHints.hint: Model every word with an action first; ask only for echo repetition this session.
Give the Hindi gloss once (skip यानी उछलकर चलना), then keep English only.
Give the Marathi gloss once (skip म्हणजे उड्या मारत चालणे), then keep English only.
Do the action yourself slowly and re-ask; never say 'wrong' — say 'Almost! Watch my feet.'
Ask for the action, not the word: 'Show me jump.' Speech follows movement.
Narrow to a choice of two: 'Is this skip or jump?' with two flashcards visible.
Ask them to be teacher: 'Tell me which action I should do.' Reversal shows real ownership.
Re-open with the two hardest pairs only (skip/jump, grin/green) in a quick game next session.

remediationStrategies: Total Physical Response loop: say word → do action → student does action → student says word.
Minimal-pair drilling with visuals for confusable pairs (skip/jump, grin/green).
Choral-then-solo speaking: whole class echoes twice, then the student alone, with applause regardless.
assessmentCriteria: Recognises at least 6 of 12 word-bank words on hearing (points/acts correctly).
Produces at least 4 word-bank words in intelligible English speech.
Joins the poem recitation for at least one line pair.
masteryIndicators: Uses an action word unprompted in a new sentence (e.g. 'I can jump.') on a later day.
Identifies the word when Miss Julie does the action silently (reversed direction).
Explains one word to a classmate in English or L1 — teaching evidence.
revisionActivities: Simon-says variant: 'Miss Julie says jump!' using the six action words.
Two-flashcard quick-fire: 60-second recognition round at the start of the next session.
entries.shortSpokenHomework: Tell someone at home one thing you do at school — in English or mixed with Hindi/Marathi. Two words are enough!

teachingStages.note: Bell sound or hidden flashcard sparks guessing: 'What is this?'
Hindi/Marathi gloss + English word, once each.
Miss Julie acts every word; students mirror.
'Show me…' and 'What is this?' checks.
Speech-recognition turn: student says a word; accept and score gently.
Re-model with mouth-shape cues, never 'wrong'.
Reversed check: Miss Julie acts, student names.
Next-session 60-second flashcard round.

review.notes: Chapter facts and word bank read directly from official printed page 1; poem is third-party credited in the book. Pedagogy fields are Talkora-original teaching design awaiting a human teacher sign-off.

copyrightStatus.reproductionRule: Title + page + word bank only; do not reproduce the rhyme text. Teach through actions and the word bank.

sourceReferences.locator: English Balbharati Grade One (2025), printed p.2, chapter 1.2 Clap your hands — action rhyme with word bank (clap, knee, buckle, shoe, turn, around, floor, dive, hands, nod, head, stamp, foot, bend) and 'For the Teacher' action-swap instruction

learningObjectives: Perform the body-action rhyme: clap hands, nod head, stamp foot, bend, turn around, touch knee/floor.
Say the 14 body/action words while doing them.
Follow one-step English instructions ('Touch your nose.', 'Blink your eyes.').
Hear and respond to number words one to five woven into the rhyme.
prerequisiteSkills: 1.1 poem words (see, play) are a soft prerequisite, not a gate.
Can point to own body parts on request.

vocabulary.sourceRef: 1.2 action list 'Touch your nose', printed p.2

phonicsConcepts: Blends st- in stamp and fl- in floor (hear the two sounds stuck together).
Number words one-two-three-four-five as sound patterns, before reading them.

grammarConcepts.concept: Imperative 'verb + your + body part' instruction pattern
grammarConcepts.childFriendlyFraming: When I say the doing-word first, it is a magic instruction — your body listens!

comprehensionGoals: Follow a spoken instruction without seeing it modelled ('Touch your knee.').
Act out the rhyme in the right order after two listenings.
speakingObjectives: Give Miss Julie one instruction using the pattern ('Clap your hands!') and check that she obeys.
Say the numbers one to five in order while clapping.

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Body-map robot
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Simple robot character whose parts light up as instructions are given; student says the instruction.

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Instruction dice
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Big soft dice with six actions; student rolls and commands the class.

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Number-action video
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Short animation pairing each number word with its action from the rhyme.

teacherExplanationExamples.en: Nod means yes with your head — like this. Now you nod!
teacherExplanationExamples.hi: Nod यानी 'हाँ' कहने के लिए सिर हिलाना — ऐसे। अब आप हिलाओ!
teacherExplanationExamples.mr: Nod म्हणजे 'हो' म्हणण्यासाठी डोके वळवणे — असे. आता तुम्ही वळवा!

teacherExplanationExamples.en: Bend over and touch the floor — fingers down, knees soft. Careful, slow bending.
teacherExplanationExamples.hi: झुककर फर्श को छुओ — उंगलियाँ नीचे, धीरे-धीरे।
teacherExplanationExamples.mr: वाकून फरसाला हात लावा — बोटं खाली, हळूहळू.

hindiExplanations: इस कविता में हमारा शरीर बोलता है — ताली, सिर, पैर, घुटना। हर शब्द के साथ एक हरकत है।
Stamp यानी पैर को ज़ोर से पटकना। Turn around यानी घूम जाना।
marathiExplanations: या कवितेत आपले शरीर बोलते — टाळी, डोके, पाय, गुडघा. प्रत्येक शब्दासोबत एक हालचाल आहे.
Stamp म्हणजे पाय ठोकणे. Turn around म्हणजे वळून जाणे.
expectedStudentAnswers: Performs the action correctly even if the word is mispronounced.
'Clap your hands!' given as a command to Miss Julie.
Numbers counted on fingers one to five.
Marathi/Hindi body-word slips: 'गुडघा' for knee — accept, gloss, re-model.

adaptiveTeachingHints.hint: Teach through mirroring only; words are absorbed from the rhyme, not demanded.
Anchor new words to body parts the child already knows in Hindi (कोहनी/हाथ).
Anchor new words to body parts known in Marathi (गुडघा/हात).
Slow-motion replay of the action with the word stretched: 'S-t-a-m-p.'
Command Miss Julie with a gesture + any sound; shape it into the word together.
Reduce to two visible actions; ask 'Clap or stamp?' before each turn.
Let them lead a 3-instruction chain for the class to follow.
Two-command warm-up next session: 'Clap, then stamp.' Chains test listening memory.

remediationStrategies: Backward chaining for the hardest instruction (buckle your shoe) — teacher does most, child does last step.
Mirror-pair practice: students face each other, one commands, one obeys, then swap.
Whisper-instructions round to sharpen careful listening.
assessmentCriteria: Follows at least 4 of 6 spoken instructions without a model.
Produces at least 5 action/body words while performing them.
Gives one grammatical instruction using 'your' correctly.
masteryIndicators: Invents a new two-step instruction chain unprompted ('Touch your nose, then turn around!').
Corrects a classmate's acted instruction by naming the right body word.
Counts one to five while clapping with no prompting, on a different day.
revisionActivities: Action-chain relay: each student adds one instruction to a growing chain.
Freeze game: rhyme music stops, Miss Julie names a word, students freeze in that pose.
entries.shortSpokenHomework: Teach one English action word to someone at home and make them do it. Tell me tomorrow what they did!

teachingStages.note: Miss Julie does a mystery action; students guess the word.
Gloss body words in L1 once, paired with touch.
Full rhyme with actions, twice.
'Touch your nose!' — obedience check without modelling.
Voice turn: student commands, app listens and confirms.
Stretched-word replay for blend errors.
Student invents an instruction for Miss Julie to obey.
Freeze-game revision in the next session.

review.notes: Word bank and teacher instructions read from official printed page 2. Pedagogy is Talkora-original draft.

sourceReferences.locator: English Balbharati Grade One (2025), printed pp.3-4, chapter 1.3 I know my alphabet — 'Look, say and trace' letter sets (Aa, Cc Ee, Mm, Nn Oo, Rr Ss, Uu Vv Ww Xx, Zz), capital/small card-matching game 'We go together', middle-'e' sound maze to Bela's home

learningObjectives: Recognise and name the sampled capital-small letter pairs (Aa, Cc, Ee, Mm, Nn, Oo, Rr, Ss, Uu, Vv, Ww, Xx, Zz).
Match a capital letter to its small letter by sound in the 'We go together' game.
Trace the letter shapes in the air and on screen.
Hear the middle 'e' sound in simple words and follow e-sound words through a picture maze.
prerequisiteSkills: Can say some letter names from KG or home.
1.1/1.2 vocabulary for picture naming during sound games.

vocabulary.sourceRef: 1.3 'tell its sound' teacher note, printed p.4

phonicsConcepts: Letter name vs letter sound distinction (B says 'bee', but its sound is /b/).
Middle-short-'e' listening: find words with /e/ in the middle (hen, pen, bed).
Air-tracing letter shapes while saying the sound.
comprehensionGoals: Pick the matching small letter when shown a capital letter (and vice versa).
Identify which picture word has the /e/ middle sound among three choices.
speakingObjectives: Say 'Big A, small a' style pairs aloud.
Say the sound of a shown letter (not just its name).

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Letter-card matching game
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Digital version of 'We go together': drag capital and small cards together; they cheer when matched.

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Bela's maze
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Touchscreen maze where only /e/-middle words light the path to Bela's home.

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Sky-writing letters
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Miss Julie traces a giant letter in the air; students copy and shout the sound.

teacherExplanationExamples.en: Every letter has a big form and a small form — like a mother and her baby. Big M and small m are the same letter!
teacherExplanationExamples.hi: हर अक्षर का बड़ा और छोटा रूप होता है — जैसे माँ और उसका बच्चा। Big M और small m एक ही अक्षर हैं!
teacherExplanationExamples.mr: प्रत्येक अक्षराचे मोठे आणि लहान रूप असते — आई आणि तिचे बाळासारखे. Big M आणि small m एकच अक्षर आहे!

teacherExplanationExamples.en: The letter's name and its sound are different friends. Listen: this is M ('em')… and it says /mmm/ like in 'mango'.
teacherExplanationExamples.hi: अक्षर का नाम और उसकी आवाज़ अलग होते हैं। सुनो: यह M है… और बोलता है /म्म्म/ जैसे 'mango' में।
teacherExplanationExamples.mr: अक्षराचे नाव आणि त्याचा आवाज वेगळे असतात. ऐका: हा M आहे… आणि म्हणतो /म्म्म/ 'mango' प्रमाणे.

hindiExplanations: हम बड़े और छोटे अक्षर जोड़ेंगे — A के साथ a, M के साथ m। जोड़ी मिलने पर वे खुश हो जाते हैं!
हर अक्षर की एक आवाज़ होती है। E की आवाज़ /ए/ — hen, pen, bed जैसे शब्दों के बीच में सुनाई देती है।
marathiExplanations: आपण मोठी आणि लहान अक्षरे जुळवू — A सोबत a, M सोबत m. जोडी सापडली की ती आनंदित होते!
प्रत्येक अक्षराचा एक आवाज असतो. E चा आवाज /ए/ — hen, pen, bed या शब्दांच्या मध्ये ऐकू येतो.
expectedStudentAnswers: Letter names only ('bee' for B) — expected at first, then shaped toward sounds.
Matching by pointing before matching by saying.
Marathi letter names slipping in (मुळाक्षरे) — accept, re-model in English.

adaptiveTeachingHints.hint: Start with 3 high-frequency pairs only (Aa, Mm, Ss); expand after success.
Map to known Devanagari shapes: 'A looks a little like अ's open mouth' — similarity talk, not equivalence claims.
Same anchor strategy with Marathi बाराखडी familiarity.
Two-card choice again; say the sound, not 'wrong': 'Listen once more — /mmm/ or /sss/?'
Accept pointing/tapping as the answer; pair the tap with the sound spoken together.
Freeze the set to two letters until three correct in a row.
Introduce the next letter set from the chapter's official set list.
Re-test only the failed pairs with the card game; keep it under two minutes.

remediationStrategies: Multisensory tracing: air-trace, then desk-trace, then say the sound — one letter at a time.
Sound-first renaming: always follow a letter name with its sound ('This is S. S says /sss/').
b/d anchoring with objects: 'b has a belly, d has a diaper' style visual anchors.
assessmentCriteria: Matches at least 5 capital-small pairs correctly.
Produces the sound (not just name) for at least 3 letters.
Follows 2 of 3 /e/-maze word choices correctly.
masteryIndicators: Self-corrects a b/d or a/e mix-up without help on a new day.
Names a letter's sound when the letter appears incidentally in another chapter's words.
Teaches a letter pair to a peer using the 'big and small' framing.
revisionActivities: 60-second letter-card sprint at the start of the next session.
Sound-hunt: find the /e/ word hidden among today's story words.
entries.shortSpokenHomework: Find one letter from the alphabet at home (on a box, a book, a door) and tell me its name and sound tomorrow.

teachingStages.note: Two cards that 'belong together' spark the matching idea.
Big/small letter framing + name vs sound.
Miss Julie matches one pair and says both forms.
'Which one goes with big A?'
Student says the pair aloud; app confirms.
Sound-focused re-modelling, two-choice when stuck.
Shuffled re-match without hints.
Letter-card sprint next session.

copyrightStatus.reproductionRule: Reference word families and patterns only; no page reproduction.

sourceReferences.locator: English Balbharati Grade One (2025), printed pp.5-6, chapter 1.4 Let us read — word families (am an as at; be he me we; if in is it; of on or), two-letter sight words (go no so by my up us), word-building (_en, _an, _in, _op, _un with can/fan/man example), and word break-down (man-mango, pen-pencil, win-window, pop-popcorn, sun-Sunday)

learningObjectives: Read two-letter word families aloud (am, an, as, at…; be, he, me, we…; if, in, is, it…; of, on, or).
Blend an initial letter onto a family ending to build new words (c-an → can, f-an → fan, m-an → man).
Break long words into two parts they already know (man-go, sun-day) — the official break-down exercise.
Read the little sight words go, no, so, by, my, up, us on sight.
prerequisiteSkills: 1.3 letter sounds for the sampled letters.
Comfort echoing 1-2 syllable words.
phonicsConcepts: Rhyme families as sound anchors: change the first sound, keep the ending (-an: can/fan/man).
Onset-rime blending: /k/ + /an/ = can.
Hearing that long words are made of known pieces (man-go).

grammarConcepts.concept: Word families are word patterns, not sentences — reading before grammar
grammarConcepts.childFriendlyFraming: Words live in families like you live in your family — they end the same way and sound like each other.

comprehensionGoals: Match a spoken built word to its picture (fan, sun).
Choose the correct first letter to turn _an into a named picture word.
speakingObjectives: Read aloud a full family row (am, an, as, at) in one breath.
Build one new word aloud by adding a first sound Miss Julie names.

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Word-family train
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Engine carries the ending (-an); wagons carry first letters; correct matches connect with a clunk.

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Word break-down magic
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Long word splits into two puzzle pieces that snap apart (sun-day, man-go).

suggestedVisualActivities.title: Sight-word balloons
suggestedVisualActivities.description: Little words (go, my, up) float by; pop them by saying them.

teacherExplanationExamples.en: Watch the magic: I put 'f' in front of '-an'… f-an… FAN! Now you try with 'c'.
teacherExplanationExamples.hi: जादू देखो: मैं 'f' को '-an' के आगे लगाती हूँ… f-an… FAN! अब तुम 'c' से करो।
teacherExplanationExamples.mr: जादू पाहा: मी 'f' ला '-an' पुढे लावते… f-an… FAN! आता तुम्ही 'c' ने करा.

teacherExplanationExamples.en: Sun-day is the sun's day — that is why we rest and play on Sunday. Sun… day… Sunday!
teacherExplanationExamples.hi: Sunday यानी सूरज का दिन — इसलिए हम रविवार को आराम करते हैं। Sun… day… Sunday!
teacherExplanationExamples.mr: Sunday म्हणजे सूर्याचा दिवस — म्हणून आपण रविवारी आराम करतो. Sun… day… Sunday!

hindiExplanations: शब्दों के परिवार — जैसे can, fan, man: आख़िरी आवाज़ एक जैसा, पहला अक्षर बदलता है।

teacherExplanationExamples.en: Now we fold — fold it in a half, then again, like the book shows. Say the step while you do it: 'Fold it in a half!'
teacherExplanationExamples.hi: अब मोड़ते हैं — आधा मोड़ो, फिर दोबारा, जैसे किताब दिखाती है। करते हुए बोलो: 'Fold it in a half!'
teacherExplanationExamples.mr: आता घडी करू — अर्ध्यात घडी करा, मग पुन्हा, पुस्तक दाखवते तसं. करताना म्हण: 'Fold it in a half!'
